content: Agastache rugosa, also known as Korean Mint, Blue Licorice, Purple Giant Hyssop, Huo Xiang (藿香) in Chinese, Indian Mint, Patchouli Herb, or Wrinkled Giant Hyssop, is a medicinal and ornamental plant belonging to the Lamiaceae family. It is also referred to by its synonym, Lophanthus rugosus Fisch. & Mey. This plant is characterized by its slightly warm nature and a spicy taste. In traditional Chinese medicine, it is associated with the Spleen (Sp), Stomach (St), and Lung (Lu) meridians. Its primary therapeutic functions include: 1. Acting as an aromatic herb that transforms dampness in the Spleen, thereby improving its function. 2. Harmonizing the middle burner (the digestive system) and alleviating vomiting. 3. Dispelling or relieving external dampness, making it particularly effective in treating conditions related to summer heat and dampness.
